correctness.rationale: For a rotation r^a, the arrow orbit has a fixed barycenter exactly when gcd(n,a)>=2: if gcd=1 the orbit is a full directed cycle and not a face; if gcd>=2, a translated set of forward arrows forms a vertex-disjoint matching. Each reflection has an invariant two-arrow matching for n>=6. The cited connectivity theorem makes X_n simply connected, so Armstrong’s orbit-space theorem gives pi1(|X_n|/H)=H/N_H where N_H is generated by elements with fixed points. For proper rotation subgroups the generator has a fixed point; for the full rotation group the fixed exponents generate <r^p> exactly when n=p^e and generate the whole group when n has distinct prime divisors; reflection-containing subgroups are generated by fixed-point reflections and, when needed, a fixed-point rotation. For prime p, the rotation action is free. The Cartan–Leray homology spectral sequence has only the b=0 row in total degrees <=(p-5)/2 because the covering complex has the cited connectivity, giving H_j(C_p;Z), which is Z/p in positive odd degrees and zero in positive even degrees. The finite verifier is only corroboration.
